entities.title: /.well-known/cyberspace.json
entities.summary: What a cooperating website may publish, and what the crawler does with it.
guarantees: cyberspace: 1 is required; a file without it is ignored and the site is read as if it had none.
A file with neither repository nor tree still counts: its related addresses and noAi sections apply while the crawler infers the site's views.
tree.files are paths ending in .json without .., at most 500; tree.base may be relative to the site.
repository must be on github.com or gitlab.com over https; it is added and crawled.
related addresses, at most 50, are added disabled until the admin allows them.
noAi paths are never sent to a model.
entities.compatibility: The version field lets a later version change the format; the crawler ignores fields it doesn't know.

entities.title: space/<id>/index.json
entities.summary: What one scan of an address left, read first by the explorer's Worker.
guarantees: kind, url, id, source (well-known, repository or inferred), label, paths (views under files/), changed, needsAi, scannedAt, reason and requests are always there.
git: ref, head, stale (views whose cited sources changed) and truncated.
web: continueFrom while a scan is unfinished; declarationError when a well-known file was rejected; repository, related and noAi for a cooperating site.
entities.compatibility: Fields are only added. A view's path is its repository path (or tree path), so the explorer reads files/ as it reads a repository.

entities.title: Scan queue message
entities.summary: What the schedule, /admin, an approaching player or a continuing scan send to cyberspace-scans.
guarantees: { id, reason } with reason schedule, admin, approach, declared, continue or ai; continue also has from. ai runs the AI step on what the last scan collected.
A message for an unknown address is acknowledged and skipped; a disabled address is skipped only when the schedule sent it.
entities.compatibility: Senders mark the address queued with store.requestScan first, so one address is never queued twice.

entities.title: The cyberspace database
guarantees: addresses, scans, fetches and settings as in crawler/schema.sql; every statement is CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, so the file can be applied again.
entities.compatibility: Columns are only added; a change is a new statement in schema.sql, applied by the owner.

entities.title: A section's reading
entities.summary: What the AI step writes about each section of an inferred website, in <section>/folder.json, for the explorer to read and Cyberspace to shape buildings with.
guarantees: The folder record's one entity has title, summary and purpose, and evidenceStatus inferred.

It also has function, family (commerce, service, content, corporate or fine_print), audience, interaction, dataSensitivity (none, personal, payment or health), lifecycle, topics (at most five), confidence (0 to 1), evidence (pages or urls_only), urls and newestLastModified.
Values outside the scheme are never written: an unknown function becomes other, unknown audiences are dropped.
entities.compatibility: Fields are only added; the scheme's values are only added to.
